content: 1. Barbiturates, including phenobarbital and shepherd's purse, both enhance sedative effects. Close monitoring and caution are advised when these agents are co-administered. 2. Siberian ginseng may potentiate the effects of phenobarbital through pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially increasing central nervous system (CNS) depression. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but caution is recommended. 3. Phenobarbital reduces the plasma levels and efficacy of sildenafil by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative therapies should be considered, as potent CYP3A4 inducers can significantly lower sildenafil concentrations. 4. Phenobarbital decreases the levels and effects of silodosin by influencing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters and CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative medications are recommended due to the seriousness of this interaction. 5. Phenobarbital reduces the levels and effects of simvastatin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 6. Phenobarbital decreases the levels and effects of siponimod by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with moderate CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 inducers is not recommended, particularly in patients with specific CYP2C9 genotypes (1/3 or 2/3). 7. Phenobarbital reduces the levels and effects of sirolimus by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporters and CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative therapies are advised. 8. Co-administration of phenobarbital and sodium oxybate is contraindicated due to pharmacodynamic synergy, which increases CNS depression. Sodium oxybate prescribing information also contraindicates its use with alcohol or insomnia drugs. 9. Phenobarbital decreases the levels and effects of sofosbuvir by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporters, reducing the conversion to its active metabolite (GS-331007). Alternative therapies are recommended. 10. Phenobarbital reduces the levels and effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs, as velpatasvir is a substrate of CYP2B6, CYP2C8, and CYP3A4. 11. Phenobarbital decreases the levels and effects of solifenacin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, belladonna alkaloids and solifenacin both reduce cholinergic transmission. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 12. Somapacitan reduces the levels and effects of phenobarbital by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Limited data suggest growth hormone treatment increases CYP450-mediated clearance. Caution is advised with sensitive CYP substrates. 13. Phenobarbital decreases the levels and effects of sonidegib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided. 14. Phenobarbital reduces the levels and effects of sorafenib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative therapies are recommended. 15. Phenobarbital decreases the levels and effects of sotagliflozin by inducing UGT1A9-mediated glucuronidation, a major metabolic pathway for this drug. Co-administration with UGT1A9 inducers may reduce sotagliflozin efficacy. 16. Phenobarbital reduces the levels and effects of sotalol by increasing its metabolism. Consider higher beta-blocker doses during co-administration, though atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less affected than other beta-blockers. 17. Phenobarbital decreases the levels and effects of sotorasib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative therapies are recommended. 18. Sparsentan increases phenobarbital levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism, while phenobarbital reduces sparsentan levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative therapies are advised. 19. Stiripentol increases phenobarbital levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism, while phenobarbital reduces stiripentol levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP1A2 metabolism. Co-administration may increase sedation risks. Alternative therapies are recommended. 20. Phenobarbital reduces streptomycin levels by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporters. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 21. Succinylcholine increases cholinergic effects, while belladonna alkaloids decrease them. The interaction's clinical significance is unclear, but caution is advised. Phenobarbital reduces succinylcholine effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. 22. Phenobarbital and sufentanil both increase sedation. Phenobarbital reduces sufentanil levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to withdrawal symptoms in dependent patients. Alternative therapies are recommended. 23. Phenobarbital reduces sulfamethoxazole levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but caution is advised. 24. Phenobarbital decreases sunitinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 25. Phenobarbital reduces suvorexant levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inducers may decrease suvorexant efficacy; if dose adjustments are needed, do not exceed 20 mg/day. 26. Phenobarbital decreases tacrolimus levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporters. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 27. Phenobarbital reduces tadalafil levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination in pulmonary hypertension patients. For erectile dysfunction, monitor tadalafil response closely. 28. Talquetamab increases phenobarbital levels by suppressing CYP enzyme activity during cytokine release syndrome (CRS). Monitor for increased phenobarbital concentrations and adjust doses as needed. 29. Phenobarbital decreases tamoxifen levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 30. Phenobarbital reduces tamsulosin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative therapies are recommended. 31. Phenobarbital and tapentadol both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 32. Phenobarbital decreases tasimelteon levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 33. Phenobarbital reduces tazemetostat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative therapies are recommended. 34. Teclistamab increases phenobarbital levels by suppressing CYP450 enzyme activity. Monitor for increased concentrations or toxicities of CYP substrates and adjust doses as needed. 35. Tecovirimat increases phenobarbital levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Monitor for adverse effects when co-administered with sensitive CYP substrates. 36. Phenobarbital and temazepam both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 37. Phenobarbital reduces temsirolimus levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 38. Phenobarbital decreases teniposide levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 39. Phenobarbital reduces terbinafine levels by inducing CYP1A2, CYP2C9/10, and CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 40. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while terbutaline decreases it. The interaction's clinical significance is unclear, but caution is advised. 41. Phenobarbital reduces tetracycline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative therapies are recommended. 42. Phenobarbital decreases tezacaftor levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative therapies are recommended. 43. Thalidomide increases phenobarbital's sedative effects through an unspecified mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 44. Phenobarbital reduces theophylline levels by inducing CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 45. Phenobarbital and thioridazine both increase sedation. Thioridazine decreases phenobarbital levels through an unspecified mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 46. Phenobarbital and thiothixene both increase sedation. Thiothixene increases belladonna alkaloid effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 47. Phenobarbital reduces thyroid desiccated levels by increasing metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but caution is advised. 48. Phenobarbital decreases tiagabine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but caution is advised.
